title: Midchain KV lock deadtime — after-action and short-term runbook
content:
Summary:
On 2026-10-02 at ~14:07 UTC we observed a sharp latency degradation and elevated 5xx rates for the hosted text-generation API in eu-west-1. Impact lasted ~27 minutes for a subset of customers and streaming connections experienced partial stalls. Root cause was a pathological KV cache lock behavior in the midchain cache shard (kv-mid-12) that caused request processing to stall under a specific concurrency pattern (short requests with high prefix-hit ratio + aggressive cache warming).

Severity and impact:
- Severity: P0 (affecting production customer SLAs)
- Surface area: ~8% of active sessions in eu-west-1 experienced token-level stalls; visible as long tail latency and ~20% spike in 500/502/504 class errors for those sessions.
- Customer-visible: truncated streaming responses for some clients, and timeouts on synchronous endpoints hitting our customer-facing latency SLO (95th percentile).

Timeline (high level):
- 14:06:38 UTC — First alert: token-latency 95th jumped from 210ms to 1250ms for route /v1/generate (eu-west-1).
- 14:07:05 UTC — SRE on-call (Maya) triaged; observed increased queue depths on midchain workers and a correlated spike in KV store lock contention metrics for shard kv-mid-12.
- 14:08:40 UTC — Temporary mitigation: routed new traffic away from kv-mid-12 by updating routing policy to prefer kv-mid-10/11 (manual failover), which lowered error rate for new requests but existing sessions remained impacted due to sticky connection to existing workers.
- 14:12:20 UTC — Engineering confirmed root cause hypothesis (lock hold-time outliers) via CPU profiles and flame graphs from the affected midchain nodes.
- 14:18:00 UTC — Rolling restart of midchain pool kv-mid-12 initiated (safe drain + restart).
- 14:28:15 UTC — Majority of sessions recovered; 5xx and latency returned near baseline.
- 14:33:00 UTC — Incident declared resolved; monitoring continued for 2 hours.

Detection and signals:
- Primary detection: latency SLO alert for route /v1/generate 95th > 1s.
- Secondary signals: KV lock contention metric (kv.lock.wait.ms) elevated on kv-mid-12; midchain worker queue depth metric > 80% of capacity; streaming session stalls flagged by session-heartbeat missing for >30s.
- Observability gaps: we had flame graphs but lacked an automated correlation between lock hold-time histograms and client session IDs which would have shortened time to precise session-level impact identification.

Root cause analysis (technical):
1) Codepath: A recent change (PR 1729) introduced a cache-warming routine that attempts to populate KV prefixes during request processing when a prefix-miss is detected. The routine synchronously acquired a per-prefix lock and, on miss, did an extend/merge operation that in some cases walked a large prefix tree.
2) Concurrency pattern: Under a particular workload seen in eu-west-1 (many short chat prompts with repeated prefixes), multiple workers contending for the same prefix lock created a convoy. The merge operation was non-idempotent and ran a relatively expensive traversal holding the lock for tens to hundreds of milliseconds.
3) Amplifier: The request router’s session-affinity meant many clients continued to hit the affected midchain workers, compounding queueing and causing downstream request timeouts.
4) Fallback logic: Our preexisting fallback to use cold fetch (bypassing the merge) was gated behind an error threshold that did not fire because the merge completed successfully but slowly — so fallback never activated.

Contributing process reasons:
- PR review missed a performance regression in the warm-path because unit tests covered correctness but not latency under contention.
- Load testing matrix did not include the specific short-request/high-prefix-hit workload that triggered the issue.
- Runbook for this class of KV contention existed but lacked a quick mitigation step to proactively reroute sessions based on lock-hold percentiles.

Immediate mitigations taken during the incident:
- Manual traffic re-routing away from kv-mid-12 (reduced new sessions to affected nodes).
- Safe rolling restart of kv-mid-12 to break the lock convoys and clear long-held mutexes.
- Short-term param change: lowered the merge-path lock hold warning threshold and enabled a conservative fallback path immediately (feature-flag toggle) to disable synchronous cache-warming under high contention.

Post-incident actions (short-term, 0–7 days):
- SRE: Add an automated reroute runbook step that triggers when kv.lock.wait.ms p95 > 50ms for a shard for more than 60s (owner: Tom Nguyen, due: 2026-10-06).
- Eng (serving-runtime): Revert or gate the synchronous merge-path in PR 1729 behind an opt-in config, and add non-blocking async warming (owner: Ravi Patel, due: 2026-10-05).
- QA: Add a targeted load test that simulates short prompt bursts with high prefix reuse to CI performance suite (owner: Elena Garcia, due: 2026-10-07).
- Product/CS: Notify top impacted customers with an incident summary and an offer to review any SLA impact (owner: Maya Thompson, due: 2026-10-06).

Longer-term remediation (30–90 days):
- Implement optimistic concurrency for prefix-warming (no global lock) or switch to per-entry fine-grained locking to reduce hold times (owner: serving-runtime team, due: 2026-11-30).
- Improve observability: correlate lock-hold histograms with session IDs and add an automated incident classifier that can propose reroute candidates (owner: observability, due: 2026-11-15).
- Add canary and perf gating to PRs that touch cache-warm/merge code paths with a mandatory contention test case (owner: release-engineering, due: 2026-11-01).

Runbook draft (quick steps to mitigate KV lock convoy):
1) Detect: alert fires when kv.lock.wait.ms p95 for a shard > 50ms for > 60s.
2) Triage: check midchain worker queue depth and recent deploy PRs affecting cache-warm paths; look up shard to AZ mapping and customer session maps.
3) Mitigate (fast path): enable route override to send new sessions to alternative midchain shards for the region (runbook script: tools/reroute-midchain.sh).
4) If stalls persist: safe drain and restart affected midchain pool nodes (use drain window 30s).
5) Temporary config toggle: flip feature-flag disable-sync-warm for the region (FF key: serving.sync_warm.disable.eu-west-1).
6) Post: set retention window for metrics to 24h and tag incident in SRE postmortem tracker.

Testing and verification plan for fixes:
- Unit + integration: add tests that measure lock hold distribution under synthetic contention.
- Load: add a scenario to the k6 suite that reproduces the short-request/high-prefix-hit workload at regional scale.
- Canary: deploy non-blocking warm-path behind canary routing for 1% of traffic and monitor kv.lock.wait.ms p95 and error budget burn rate for 72h.

Communications:
- Incident timeline and summary posted to #sre-incidents with links to this doc and to Confluence page above.
- Customer comms draft prepared and reviewed with CS (ticket SRE-4821-commms).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Exact reason why lock hold-time outliers occurred in the first place — is it a pathological data shape in the prefix tree or an algorithmic worst-case? (action: micro-benchmark the merge traversal, owner: Ravi, due: 2026-10-12).
- Should session-affinity be relaxed during regional overloads? Requires product/architect review for trade-offs.

Appendix (observability snippets):
- Short example query used during triage: 
  - sum(rate(kv_lock_wait_seconds_count{shard="kv-mid-12"}[1m])) by (le) and histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(kv_lock_wait_seconds_bucket{shard="kv-mid-12"}[1m]))
- Flame graph artifacts uploaded to: https://storage.redwood.internal/artifacts/kv-mid-12-flame-2026-10-02.svg

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally concise. Please add missing owner assignments or timing conflicts via inline comments in Confluence page linked above. We'll convert to a formal postmortem if any customers request an RPO-level SLA review.
